cells.tense: You are at the abundant result, and your hands are still adjusting the next detail.
cells.ask: Name one thing that is done, say it's done, and take the rest of the hour off from it.
cells.core:
Something you built holds — a routine, a room, work that carries weight — and you're still reading it closely enough to catch what needs more and what needs less. You move between them without making a show of it. That's the working version, not a lack of ambition.

Because the making is finished, letting go can land as reward instead of loss. So name one finished thing as finished, and take the hour back. Keeping this steady costs something: you sit inside the full result without adding to it. That's harder than producing, and it's the actual proof that there's abundance here.
cells.sheetLine: The result is here. Stop adding to it for one hour.
cells.verb: bringing what was carefully grown through structure into finished abundance
cells.place: a place of live adjustment — adding and pulling back as the thing in front of you changes

cells.tense: You are managing the harvest that hasn't come in yet while this season's crop is still on the table.
cells.ask: Pick one finished thing and stop there for today, even if a better version is still possible.
cells.core:
The results are still arriving, and you're ahead of them — sketching next year's improvements, catching the flaw in the thing you already handed over, holding a picture of how it should go that keeps getting corrected. The attention is real. It's pointed at what's next, so what's in front of you gets less of it than it deserves.

Pick one finished thing and stop at finished for today. The way back asks you to let one result be complete in its current form, with no correction attached. That's the cost of moving back: one finished thing you don't improve tonight.
cells.sheetLine: You're working on next year while this one's already good.

cells.tense: What you grew is here with you, and the door you're standing at is one you've already walked through.
cells.ask: Show one finished piece of work to one person this week and stay in the room while they look at it.
cells.core:
There's something real under you — meals made, a habit kept, a thing built that still stands. It's just hard to stand on it in the present. When it comes up, it lands as what used to happen or what hasn't happened yet, and the small adjustments that keep it going don't get made. What's out of reach isn't the making. It's the showing.

Put one finished thing in front of one person and stay there while they take it in. The light comes after something gets seen, not before. The way back is to let that happen and stay for it. It costs a minute of being looked at, and that minute is the whole ask.
cells.sheetLine: What you made is finished. Put it where one person can see.
cells.verb: bringing what was carefully grown through structure into finished abundance

cells.tense: You are making the small adjustments hour by hour and calling the result just how it worked out.
cells.ask: Say one adjustment is yours out loud — 'I did that' — about something today you would usually let pass as ordinary.
cells.core:
You notice what needs more and what needs less, and you move it without ceremony. That's steady, ongoing, mostly invisible work. When it does come up, you hand the credit around — the timing was good, things fell into place — and the part you played doesn't get named.

The softer move is to say one adjustment is yours: the call you made, the hour you held open, the thing you left alone on purpose. Say it to somebody if they're there, and say it once before you sleep if they're not. The cost is only the claim, and the claim is true.
cells.sheetLine: You made that adjustment. Say so out loud once.

attempts.check: The unsupported move is saying what the person already knows or already did — I have only the status, so I keep any of that as a first-person option the reader can decline. The likely objection is 'you're telling me what I feel' — the asks therefore stand alone as actions the person can test whether or not my read is right. The line that serves me more than them is any tidy claim that the person's quiet or caution 'is' a wound or a forgetting; I've cut all of that and left only what the status holds.
